title: Timescales of discovering vs. learning math

cues.en: You know, one of the many really interesting things about math is that it's really, really, really
cues.zh: 你知道，數學有很多有趣的地方，其中之一就是，

cues.en: difficult to discover new principles in mathematics, but it's not that hard to learn an established principle.
cues.zh: 要發現新的數學原理真的非常困難，但學會已經確立的原理卻沒有那麼難。

cues.en: Imagine that this is a timeline that spans a billion years.
cues.zh: 想像這是一條橫跨十億年的時間軸。

cues.en: And now consider this It took nature about a billion years of evolution here on Earth to go from the
cues.zh: 再想想：大自然在地球上大約演化了十億年，才從

cues.en: beginning of life to the discovery of calculus.
cues.zh: 生命的起源走到微積分的發現。

cues.en: A billion years.
cues.zh: 十億年。

cues.en: And it took human civilization thousands of years for the right geniuses to come along and make these discoveries.
cues.zh: 而人類文明也花了幾千年，才等到合適的天才出現，做出這些發現。

cues.en: And even when those geniuses appeared, it took them years to decades to discover principles of mathematics
cues.zh: 即使這些天才出現了，他們也得花上幾年到幾十年，才能發現數學原理，

cues.en: or to invent them.
cues.zh: 或者說發明這些原理。

cues.en: That's actually a discussion for another tangent lecture.
cues.zh: 這其實是另一堂岔題課要討論的問題。

cues.en: The point that I'm trying to make is that exceedingly few humans are intellectually capable of discovering
cues.zh: 我想說的是，只有極少數人有足夠的智力，能夠完全從零開始，

cues.en: the techniques that you are learning in this course completely from scratch.
cues.zh: 發現你在這門課裡學到的技巧。

cues.en: I'm definitely not smart enough to discover these techniques.
cues.zh: 我肯定沒有聰明到能發現這些技巧。

cues.en: And no offense, of course, but I guess you're probably also not smart enough to discover calculus on your own, otherwise you wouldn't be in this course.
cues.zh: 當然沒有冒犯的意思，不過我猜你可能也沒有聰明到能自己發現微積分，不然你就不會來上這門課了。

cues.en: But.
cues.zh: 不過，

cues.en: But now that calculus is established, almost anyone can learn it and it takes only a few months.
cues.zh: 現在微積分已經確立，幾乎任何人都能學會，而且只需要幾個月。

cues.en: I mean, that is truly amazing.
cues.zh: 我是說，這真的很驚人。

cues.en: The difference between what it takes to discover something versus what it takes to learn something that is already discovered.
cues.zh: 發現某件事所需的努力，和學習已被發現的事所需的努力，差異就是這麼大。

cues.en: And why am I saying all this?
cues.zh: 我為什麼要說這些呢？

cues.en: Well, partly I think it's just interesting and thought provoking to think about intellectual achievements
cues.zh: 一部分是因為，我覺得用這些不同的時間尺度思考人類的智力成就，

cues.en: on these different time scales, but also because one of the things that makes math so frustrating to
cues.zh: 很有趣，也引人深思。另一個原因是，學數學很容易感到挫折，

cues.en: learn is that you see a proof or a demonstration or a trick for solving a particular type of problem
cues.zh: 因為你看到一個證明、示範，或解某類題目的技巧，

cues.en: and you feel like you're not smart enough to have come up with that trick on your own and therefore you're not smart enough to learn math.
cues.zh: 就覺得自己不夠聰明，不可能自己想出這個技巧，所以也不夠聰明學會數學。

cues.en: That is a really common thing to think, but it's wrong.
cues.zh: 這種想法很常見，但它是錯的。

cues.en: Like I said, it takes true geniuses years to discover these tricks in the first place, and then everyone
cues.zh: 就像我說的，真正的天才也要花好幾年，才會首次發現這些技巧，而其他所有人，

cues.en: else, including you and me, gets to benefit from their discoveries.
cues.zh: 包括你我，都可以受惠於他們的發現。

cues.en: So as you go through this course, don't worry about whether you can or can't re derive everything from scratch.
cues.zh: 所以上這門課時，不用擔心自己能不能把一切從頭重新推導出來。

cues.en: Instead, just focus on learning what other people have already figured out.
cues.zh: 專心學習別人已經弄清楚的事情就好。
